neighbours.label: the opening of a quoted or named campaign, slogan or programme title (the opening quote mark or first letter of the name)
fire: Volunteers handed out flyers for the library's “Read Across Town” challenge this summer.
The utility company asked customers to join its "Power Down Hour" every Thursday evening.
Students raised money through the school's “Pennies for Patients” drive in March.
The park service thanked campers who were “Leave No Trace” certified this year.
The health department kicked off its "Walk to Wellness" campaign at the town fair.
Thousands of drivers have signed the state's “Arrive Alive” pledge since January.
Local businesses joined the "Shop Small Saturday" event to attract holiday shoppers.
The fire department promoted its “Change Your Clock, Change Your Battery” reminder again.
quiet: Volunteers handed out flyers for the library's reading challenge across town this summer.
The utility company asked customers to use less power for an hour every Thursday evening.
Students raised money for sick children through a coin drive at school in March.
The park service thanked campers who cleaned up after themselves this year.
The health department kicked off its walking campaign at the town fair.
Thousands of drivers have promised to drive safely since January.
Local businesses held a special sale to attract holiday shoppers on Saturday.

notes: Card: peaks on the opening quote of “Take a bite out of crime”, "Great Central U.S. Shakeout", “Bear Aware”, and on 'P' of P.A.C.E. program. Near misses describe the same campaigns without giving them a quoted name.
